entries.heading: What the protocol is
entries.text: Atomicals mints digital objects on Bitcoin through a commit and reveal pattern. The commit pays into a taproot script containing an atom envelope; the reveal spends it, exposing an operation code and CBOR payload in witness data.

entries.heading: Lifecycle and status
entries.text: Atomicals activated on Bitcoin mainnet at height 808080 and evolved through dated activation heights up to custom coloring at 848484. Bitcoin Universe operates a pinned fork of atomicals-electrumx as its indexing authority.

entries.heading: Source, products, and reporting
entries.text: Owning repository, the docs.bitcoinuniverse.io portal, Bitcoin Universe products supporting these protocols, upstream Atomicals project origin, and security reporting.

entries.heading: The atom envelope
entries.text: A witness element of at least 39 bytes beginning with a 32 byte push; the parser scans to the first OP_IF and requires the five byte marker 0461746f6d, a four byte push of ASCII atom, followed by the operation push and CBOR payload pushes up to OP_ENDIF.

entries.heading: CBOR payload
entries.text: The payload must decode as a single CBOR map. The reserved keys meta, args, ctx, and init must be maps, with byte strings restricted. Functional parameters live under args, including request_ticker, mint_amount, max_mints, bitworkc, and bitworkr.

entries.heading: Identifiers
entries.text: An atomical id is 36 bytes: the commit transaction id plus the commit output index, compact form txid i index. A location id names where the atomical currently sits. Mints imprint at output 0 of the reveal.

entries.heading: Commit and reveal
entries.text: Mint operations must ride input 0. The commit must be indexed and at or after height 808080. General reveals must occur within 100 blocks of the commit; name mints within 3 blocks. From height 822800 the commit outpoint index must be 0 for name type and dmt mints.

entries.heading: Operations
entries.text: Recognized operation codes: nft, ft, dft, dmt, mod, evt, dat, sl, x splat, y split, z custom color, plus the fork's AVM def and new. Each has a fixed push encoding in the envelope.

entries.heading: ARC-20 issuance
entries.text: Tickers must match a-z0-9 of 1 to 21 characters and resolve by earliest commit. Direct ft mints set supply from reveal output 0. Decentralized dft deploys declare mint_amount, max_mints, and mint_height; dmt claims must pay exactly mint_amount to output 0.

entries.heading: Bitwork proof-of-work
entries.text: A bitwork string is a hex prefix with an optional fractional extension 0 to 15, such as 123af.15. The transaction id must start with the prefix and the next digit must be at least the extension. Perpetual dmint difficulty rises after every max_mints claims.

entries.heading: ARC-20 coloring rules
entries.text: Tokens are ordered first in first out by input index, then color outputs left to right, skipping OP_RETURN. From height 848484 the last output touched may be partially colored. Value landing on no spendable output burns. A failed placement restarts every token from output 0.

entries.heading: State, sealing, immutability
entries.text: The mod operation updates state by recursive merge, or deletes keys when the payload sets a dollar-a of 1. Immutable NFTs never accept mod or evt. The sl operation permanently seals an NFT so it can never move or change.

entries.heading: Realms, containers, dmitems
entries.text: Realm names match a-z followed by a-z0-9 and hyphens up to 64 characters. Top level names require commit bitwork of at least four hex characters. Subrealms use direct or rule claims with a payment window from commit plus 3 to commit plus 15 blocks. Containers publish a merkle root that dmitem mints prove against.

entries.heading: Activation heights
entries.text: Bitcoin mainnet activation heights: 808080 activation, 819181 dmint and FIFO ordering, 822800 commitz, 828128 density, 828628 bitwork rollover, 848484 custom coloring, 900000 AVM.

entries.heading: Invalidity conditions
entries.text: Envelope structural failures, mint placement failures, name failures, deploy parameter failures, claim failures, payment failures, and unmet bitwork. Coloring never fails a transaction: invalid intent shows up as burned or unmoved value, not a rejected transaction.

entries.heading: The mental model
entries.text: An ARC-20 balance is a set of satoshis, not a ledger entry. Holding 10000 units means holding a 10000 satoshi UTXO recorded as colored. Coin selection is therefore dangerous and output order decides everything.

entries.heading: How a mint happens
entries.text: Every Atomical is created by two transactions: a commit that pays into a taproot script containing the envelope, and a reveal that spends it. Commit and reveal exists so name claims cannot be front run.

entries.heading: Launching an ARC-20 token
entries.text: Direct mints create the whole supply at once from the reveal's first output. Decentralized mints declare mint_amount, max_mints, mint_height and optional bitwork, then anyone may claim in a public race.

entries.heading: How a transfer colors outputs
entries.text: Collect the token pool across inputs, order tokens FIFO, fill outputs left to right, and anything left over burns. A transfer is engineered by choosing output values; the order matters more than the addresses.

entries.heading: Worked transactions
entries.text: A clean split, paying the fee from plain bitcoin instead of colored value, and separating two tokens sharing one UTXO with the split operation.

entries.heading: Pitfalls that destroy value
entries.text: Fee funded from a colored input, an output too small for the remaining balance, sending to a service that does not index Atomicals, consolidating UTXOs, ordinary wallet coin selection, and directing value at an OP_RETURN output under z.

entries.heading: Product support matrix
entries.text: Which actions Bitcoin Universe products support for ARC-20, Atomicals NFTs, realms, and subrealms across marketplace, wallet, and Inscribe, limited to what is verifiable in code, with the single host order book durability limit and open settlement reorg reconciliation stated.

entries.heading: Terminology
entries.text: Atomical, ARC-20, envelope, commit and reveal, atomical id, location id, coloring, sat value and atomical value, cleanly assigned, burn, bitwork, dft and dmt, splat and split, realm, sealed.

entries.heading: Indexer semantics
entries.text: Deterministic ordering by position, confirmation depths including the 3 block name verification depth, provisional mempool state and replace-by-fee consequences, and exact reorg rollback from per block undo data within the retained reorg limit.

entries.heading: Universe indexing decisions
entries.text: Where this documentation follows the Bitcoin Universe indexers rather than upstream Atomicals documentation: envelope prefix tolerance, AVM operations, split transaction payment refusal, the two repository split, and marketplace fail closed reads.

entries.heading: Fee and size considerations
entries.text: Two transactions per mint, witness discounted payloads, token value locked as satoshi value, dust limits and the 546 satoshi minimum mint amount, bitwork costing time rather than fees, and fee funding that burns tokens.

entries.heading: Limitations
entries.text: No divisibility or decimals at the protocol layer, supply bounded by immobilized bitcoin, no protocol level rejection, ordering that couples unrelated assets, ASCII only names, slowed upstream development, and low indexer diversity.

entries.heading: Security considerations
entries.text: Coin selection as the primary risk, validating before signing, verifying ownership at the exact outpoint, failing closed on indexer outage, respecting the 3 block name depth, reconciling after reorgs, and treating payload content as untrusted.

entries.heading: Implementation checklist
entries.text: The minimum work to index or integrate correctly: envelope parsing, input 0 enforcement, commit windows, identity derivation, exact coloring, split and custom color semantics, NFT movement, deploy bounds and cap recounting, bitwork, name races, undo data, and exposing burns.

entries.heading: Valid coloring
entries.text: Exact single output, ordinary two way split, uncolored change beyond the pool, two tokens in FIFO order with clean boundaries, the non-clean fallback, and a partially colored input carried forward.

entries.heading: Burn cases
entries.text: A remainder with nowhere to go burning 10000 units, an output larger than the remaining balance burning everything under exact cover rules, one unit over, a fee taken from colored value, and no outputs able to take color.

entries.heading: Split and custom color
entries.text: Merged inputs into a single output, split skip amounts, custom color with over request clamping, custom color leaving value unassigned, and a transaction with no atomicals at all.

entries.heading: Envelope parsing
entries.text: Valid marker, short element, wrong first byte, wrong marker, unknown operation, payload not a map, undecodable payload, bytes in meta, and an empty tapscript.

entries.heading: Mint validity
entries.text: Valid direct mint and dmt claim, wrong claim amount, premature claim, cap exceeded, envelope on input 1, late reveal, late named reveal, nonzero commit index, out of range deploy, immutable fungible, and two name requests.

entries.heading: Bitwork
entries.text: Prefix match and mismatch, fractional extension satisfied and not satisfied, an extension of zero, malformed hex and out of range extension, difficulty target calculation, and a perpetual phase step.

entries.heading: Names and tickers
entries.text: Valid and invalid tickers and realms, short bitwork on a top level name, a claim race decided by earliest commit, a late subname payment, a payment inside a split transaction, and a malformed dmitem merkle proof.

entries.heading: ARC-20 transfer outcome simulator
entries.text: Enter inputs carrying token color and output values; the page applies the indexer's coloring rules client side and explains step by step which outputs carry which balance and when color burns. Nothing entered is logged or transmitted.

entries.heading: What this instrument models
entries.text: Regular transfers, the non-clean fallback, split skip amounts, custom color clamping, and burn accounting, across the exact cover and partial coloring eras.
